summary: RFC 7589 protects NETCONF messages with TLS 1.2. This document updates it with revised TLS 1.2 support requirements and TLS 1.3 requirements, including limits on TLS 1.3 early data.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC updates how NETCONF uses TLS to protect messages. It adds TLS 1.3 rules, prohibits early data and keeps the other connection rules from RFC 7589.

questions: does netconf over tls support tls 1.3
is early data allowed in netconf over tls
what port does netconf over tls use
subtitle: NETCONF updates TLS support requirements and prohibits TLS 1.3 early data.

tldr.problem: RFC 7589 described NETCONF over TLS 1.2 but did not define TLS 1.3 support requirements or early-data restrictions.
tldr.mechanism: Implementations must support mutually authenticated TLS 1.2, should support TLS 1.3, and must not use early data with TLS 1.3 or later.
tldr.outcome: The RFC updates RFC 7589 and updates the registry reference for the netconf-tls service.

today: RFC 9918 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2026. It updates RFC 7589; the unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 9918.

sections.title: Changes to NETCONF over TLS
sections.content:
RFC 7589 defines how to protect Network Configuration Protocol (NETCONF) messages with TLS 1.2. RFC 9918 updates TLS 1.2 support requirements and adds TLS 1.3 requirements, including limits on early data.

It also updates the IANA registry entry for netconf-tls. Other provisions of RFC 7589 remain unchanged, including connection initiation, message framing, closure, certificate validation and client and server identity.
sections.plainLanguage: NETCONF messages use TLS for protection. This update adds TLS 1.3 requirements and changes the registry reference, but keeps the other connection rules.

sections.title: Early Data Is Prohibited
sections.content:
Early data, also called 0-RTT data, lets a TLS 1.3 client send data in its first flight of messages. It is allowed only when the client and server share a Pre-Shared Key. TLS 1.3 can be used without early data.

Early data is not forward secret and has no protection against replay between connections. Therefore, NETCONF implementations supporting TLS 1.3 or later MUST NOT use early data.
sections.plainLanguage: Early data is sent before later TLS-protected data and can be replayed between connections. NETCONF implementations using TLS 1.3 or later must not send it.

sections.title: TLS Versions and Cipher Suites
sections.content:
Implementations MUST support mutually authenticated TLS 1.2. They SHOULD support mutually authenticated TLS 1.3, and must prefer TLS 1.3 over earlier versions if they implement it. TLS 1.3 implementations are required to support the cipher suites listed as mandatory in Section 9.1 of RFC 9846.

The RFC also discusses optional cipher suites that provide mutual authentication and confidentiality. NETCONF over TLS requires mutual authentication, and peers should not connect to an unknown, unexpected or incorrectly identified peer.
sections.plainLanguage: Implementations must support mutually authenticated TLS 1.2 and should support TLS 1.3. If TLS 1.3 is supported, it must be preferred over earlier TLS versions.

sections.title: The netconf-tls Registry Entry
sections.content: IANA added a reference to RFC 9918 in the netconf-tls entry of the Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry. The entry names port 6513 over TCP and describes the service as NETCONF over TLS.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry entry for NETCONF over TLS now cites this RFC as well as RFC 7589. The listed port and transport are 6513 and TCP.
